newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge to rule soon in assisted-suicide case.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge to rule soon in assisted-suicide case.

text.p: A judge said on Tuesday she will rule within a week whether a dying AIDS patient will be allowed to take his own life in a physician-assisted suicide.

Charles Hall, 35, continued his legal quest to win the right to physician-assisted suicide with a petition to Palm Beach Circuit Judge Lucy Brown, asking her to lift a court order imposed after he persuaded another judge to allow his doctor to help him die.

After hearing arguments from Hall's lawyer and an attorney for the state of Florida, Brown said she would rule within a week. Hall's doctor, Jupiter, Florida physician Cecil McIver, said he thought his ailing patient might live long enough to hear the ruling.
"I think he could survive a week," McIver said at the courthouse.
Hall, unable to leave his Beverly Hills, Florida, home as he battled AIDS-related pneumonia, listened to the hearing by telephone.

Last week Palm Beach County Judge Joseph Davis ruled Hall had the right to take his own life with the assistance of a doctor. But Florida, which opposed Hall, announced it would appeal, triggering a stay.
Hall's attorney, Robert Rivas, told the court there was "no logic" to the state's continued opposition.
"Death is not a condition which can be reversed by any legal authority. There is no chance that a cure for AIDS will be found before he dies," Rivas said.

Arguing for the state, which signalled its intent to have the Florida Supreme Court hear the issue, assistant attorney-general Parker Thomson said Florida had a broader interest in the case -- to protect the disabled, elderly and others from abuse.
"The state has a right to have these issues decided once and for all," Thomson said.
Rivas said Hall was refusing treatment because he knew it would not alter the course of his disease and was able to take only limited nourishment.
